{{Short description|Mathematical function}}
In [[mathematics]], '''conical functions''' or '''Mehler functions''' are [[function (mathematics)|functions]] which can be expressed in terms of [[Legendre function]]s of the first and second kind,
<math>P^\mu_{-(1/2)+i\lambda}(x)</math> and <math>Q^\mu_{-(1/2)+i\lambda}(x).</math>

The functions <math>P^\mu_{-(1/2)+i\lambda}(x)</math> were introduced by [[Gustav Ferdinand Mehler]], in 1868, when expanding in series the distance of a point on the axis of a cone to a point located on the surface of the cone. Mehler used the notation <math>K^\mu(x)</math> to represent these functions. He obtained integral representation and series of functions representations for them. He also established an addition theorem
for the conical functions. [[Carl Neumann]] obtained an expansion of the functions <math>K^\mu(x)</math> in terms
of the [[Legendre polynomials]] in 1881. Leonhardt introduced for the conical functions the equivalent of the [[spherical harmonics]] in 1882.
